title: Only 8% Pass This Paramedic Entrance Exam
summary: Scene safety, vital signs, emergency maths and rapid-response judgement combine in one focused entrance challenge.

landing.intro: From scene hazards and vital signs to emergency maths and calm communication, prove you can think clearly when every clue matters.

startPrompt.title: Assessment Ready 🚑
startPrompt.copy: Watch a short ad to start the test.

questions.question: Which route correctly follows oxygen into the circulation?
questions.explanation: Air travels through the airway to the lungs, where oxygen crosses into the blood.

questions.question: How much time passes from 14:35 to 15:20?
questions.explanation: There are 25 minutes to 15:00 and another 20 minutes to 15:20, making 45 minutes.

questions.question: How should the floor hazard be handled first?

visual.ariaLabel: Used sharp, broken glass and a clear exit

answers: Isolate the hazard and report it
questions.explanation: Sharps should not be handled casually; isolate the hazard and use an appropriately trained safe-disposal process.

questions.question: Which measurement changed while the others stayed the same?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse unchanged, breathing increased, alertness unchanged, skin warmth unchanged

questions.explanation: Breathing increased from 16 to 25 while the remaining observations stayed unchanged.

questions.question: A person keeps nodding but has not understood. What should happen next?
answers: Use plain words and check back
questions.explanation: Clear language, appropriate communication support and a check-back confirm whether the message was understood.

questions.question: Who takes priority?

items: B · NEW BREATHING DIFFICULTY · CANNOT FINISH A SENTENCE
visual.ariaLabel: Person A is comfortable and asks for a blanket. Person B has new breathing difficulty and cannot finish a sentence.

questions.explanation: New breathing difficulty severe enough to limit speech is the immediate priority.

questions.question: Which change is the strongest warning of deterioration?
questions.explanation: New confusion is a major change from baseline, while the other values are unchanged or only minimally different.

questions.question: Which detail is most urgent to hand over?

visual.ariaLabel: Vehicle stopped, two people, strong fuel smell

answers: The fuel smell and possible ignition hazard
questions.explanation: A strong fuel smell may indicate an immediate scene hazard and must be communicated clearly.

questions.question: Who needs attention first?

items: PERSON A · SORE WRIST · NORMAL SPEECH · STEADY OBSERVATIONS
PERSON B · COLLAPSED · PALE · RAPID BREATHING · NEW CONFUSION
visual.ariaLabel: Person A has a sore wrist, normal speech and steady observations. Person B collapsed and is pale, breathing rapidly and newly confused.

questions.explanation: Person B has multiple time-sensitive signs across several systems, making them the clear priority.

details.tipsTitle: Three ways to sharpen your response thinking
details.tipsIntro: These are general quiz strategies—not clinical instruction, medical advice or a professional assessment.

tips.title: Scan for immediate danger
tips.copy: Before interpreting finer details, identify hazards, sudden deterioration and airway or breathing concerns.

tips.title: Compare with the baseline
tips.copy: A change from the earlier record can matter more than memorising one isolated number.

tips.title: Use every visible clue
tips.copy: Build the answer from the complete scene rather than letting one dramatic detail decide everything.

about.body:
This Rapid Response Assessment condenses entrance-level paramedic knowledge into one focused ten-question challenge. It covers anatomy and physiology, emergency numeracy, observation trends, scene safety, calm communication, handover and multi-clue prioritisation.

The challenge is designed for curious adults, prospective paramedic students and emergency-care learners around the world. It uses universal principles such as recognising immediate hazards, noticing deterioration, protecting dignity, communicating clearly and seeking appropriately qualified help—never country-specific protocols or specialist treatment decisions.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the entrance areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of clinical competence or suitability for paramedic practice.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer ten varied response questions and choose the single option best supported by the visible information.
Correct answers stay hidden while you play, so inspect every scene clue, timeline, trend and handover carefully.
Finish the assessment to reveal your Paramedic Score, strongest entrance area and complete result report.
